cards.front: Which adverse effects set cimetidine apart from the other H2 blockers?
cards.back: All H2 blockers block **H2 receptors on parietal cells**. Only **cimetidine** is a strong **CYP450 inhibitor** (raises warfarin, phenytoin, theophylline levels) and is **antiandrogenic**: **gynecomastia**, **impotence**, low libido. It also crosses the **placenta** and blood-brain barrier (confusion in older adults).
cards.back_pt: Todos os bloqueadores H2 bloqueiam **receptores H2 das células parietais**. Só a **cimetidina** é um forte **inibidor do CYP450** (eleva os níveis de varfarina, fenitoína, teofilina) e é **antiandrogênica**: **ginecomastia**, **impotência**, redução da libido. Também atravessa a **placenta** e a barreira hematoencefálica (confusão em idosos).

cards.front: What is the key adverse effect of each type of antacid?
cards.back: **Aluminum hydroxide**: **constipation**, **hypophosphatemia**, osteodystrophy. **Magnesium hydroxide**: **diarrhea**; in renal failure, hypermagnesemia (hyporeflexia, hypotension, cardiac arrest). **Calcium carbonate**: **hypercalcemia**, rebound acid, **milk-alkali syndrome**.
cards.back_pt: **Hidróxido de alumínio**: **constipação**, **hipofosfatemia**, osteodistrofia. **Hidróxido de magnésio**: **diarreia**; na insuficiência renal, hipermagnesemia (hiporreflexia, hipotensão, parada cardíaca). **Carbonato de cálcio**: **hipercalcemia**, rebote ácido, **síndrome leite-álcali**.

cards.front: How does sucralfate protect an ulcer, and why should it not be taken with a PPI or antacid?
cards.back: In **acid**, sucralfate forms a sticky gel that **binds the ulcer base** and acts as a **physical barrier** against acid and pepsin. Drugs that raise gastric pH stop this activation. It contains **aluminum**.
cards.back_pt: Em meio **ácido**, o sucralfato forma um gel aderente que **se liga à base da úlcera** e atua como **barreira física** contra ácido e pepsina. Medicamentos que elevam o pH gástrico impedem essa ativação. Contém **alumínio**.

cards.front: What are the main uses of octreotide, and what is its classic adverse effect?
cards.back: A **somatostatin analog**. Uses: **acute variceal bleeding** (lowers splanchnic blood flow), **carcinoid syndrome**, **VIPoma**, **acromegaly**. It reduces gallbladder contraction, so it can cause **gallstones**; also nausea, cramps and steatorrhea.
cards.back_pt: **Análogo da somatostatina**. Usos: **sangramento agudo de varizes** (reduz o fluxo sanguíneo esplâncnico), **síndrome carcinoide**, **VIPoma**, **acromegalia**. Reduz a contração da vesícula biliar e pode causar **cálculos biliares**; também náusea, cólicas e esteatorreia.

cards.front: How does ondansetron prevent vomiting, and what are its adverse effects?
cards.back: It blocks **5-HT3 receptors** on vagal afferents in the gut and in the **chemoreceptor trigger zone**. It works well for chemotherapy and postoperative nausea. Adverse effects: **headache**, **constipation**, **QT prolongation**; **serotonin syndrome** with other serotonergic drugs.
cards.back_pt: Bloqueia **receptores 5-HT3** nas aferências vagais do intestino e na **zona de gatilho quimiorreceptora**. Funciona bem na náusea da quimioterapia e no pós-operatório. Efeitos adversos: **cefaleia**, **constipação**, **prolongamento do QT**; **síndrome serotoninérgica** com outros serotoninérgicos.

cards.front: How does lactulose lower ammonia in hepatic encephalopathy?
cards.back: Colonic bacteria break lactulose into **organic acids**. The acid lumen converts **NH3 to NH4+**, which is trapped and lost in stool; it is also an **osmotic laxative**. **Rifaximin**, a poorly absorbed antibiotic, is added to reduce ammonia-producing bacteria.
cards.back_pt: As bactérias do cólon degradam a lactulose em **ácidos orgânicos**. O lúmen ácido converte **NH3 em NH4+**, que fica retido e é eliminado nas fezes; também é um **laxante osmótico**. A **rifaximina**, antibiótico pouco absorvido, é associada para reduzir as bactérias produtoras de amônia.

cards.front: How do loperamide and diphenoxylate stop diarrhea, and when should they be avoided?
cards.back: They are **mu-opioid agonists** that slow gut motility; loperamide barely enters the brain. Avoid them in **bloody or invasive infectious diarrhea**, *C. difficile* colitis and severe **IBD flares**, because they can cause **toxic megacolon**.
cards.back_pt: São **agonistas opioides mu** que reduzem a motilidade intestinal; a loperamida quase não entra no cérebro. Evitar na **diarreia infecciosa invasiva ou sanguinolenta**, na colite por *C. difficile* e em **crises graves de DII**, pois podem causar **megacólon tóxico**.

cards.front: Why is allopurinol dangerous in a patient with IBD who takes azathioprine or 6-mercaptopurine?
cards.back: Azathioprine becomes **6-MP**, a purine analog. **Xanthine oxidase** inactivates 6-MP. **Allopurinol** blocks this enzyme, so 6-MP builds up and causes **bone marrow suppression**. Low **TPMT** activity has the same effect.
cards.back_pt: A azatioprina se converte em **6-MP**, um análogo de purina. A **xantina oxidase** inativa a 6-MP. O **alopurinol** bloqueia essa enzima, a 6-MP se acumula e causa **mielossupressão**. Atividade baixa de **TPMT** tem o mesmo efeito.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old woman has had muscle cramps and a hand tremor for 2 weeks. She has taken omeprazole for reflux for 7 years. She takes no diuretics, does not drink alcohol, eats a normal diet, and has no diarrhea. Inflating a blood pressure cuff on her arm causes carpal spasm. Serum calcium is 7.4 mg/dL, magnesium is 0.8 mg/dL, and creatinine is normal. Her PTH is inappropriately low for the calcium level. Urinary magnesium excretion is very low. Which mechanism best explains her low magnesium?
choices: Increased renal magnesium loss in the thick ascending limb
Shift of magnesium into cells after insulin release
Decreased active magnesium absorption in the intestine
Magnesium loss in stool from Clostridioides difficile colitis
Low magnesium intake from a poor diet
questions.explanation: Long-term **proton pump inhibitors** can impair **active intestinal magnesium absorption**, causing **hypomagnesemia**. Low magnesium reduces **PTH release** and PTH action, so **hypocalcemia** follows. The most tempting distractor is renal magnesium wasting, but the kidney is saving magnesium here (very low urinary magnesium) and she takes no loop diuretic. Other long-term PPI risks include fractures, *C. difficile* infection, pneumonia, and low iron and B12 absorption.
questions.explanation_pt: O uso prolongado de **inibidores da bomba de prótons** pode prejudicar a **absorção intestinal ativa de magnésio**, causando **hipomagnesemia**. O magnésio baixo reduz a **liberação de PTH** e a ação do PTH, levando à **hipocalcemia**. O distrator mais tentador é a perda renal de magnésio, mas aqui o rim está conservando magnésio (magnésio urinário muito baixo) e ela não usa diurético de alça. Outros riscos do IBP prolongado incluem fraturas, infecção por *C. difficile*, pneumonia e menor absorção de ferro e B12.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes has early satiety and recurrent vomiting. A gastric emptying study shows delayed emptying, and she starts a prokinetic drug. Two days later, she comes to the emergency department because her neck is twisted to one side and her eyes are fixed upward. She cannot correct these positions. Temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 84/min, and blood pressure is 118/74 mm Hg. She has no muscle rigidity, no clonus, and no diarrhea. Which mechanism best explains these new symptoms?
choices: Blockade of dopamine D2 receptors in the nigrostriatal pathway
Blockade of serotonin 5-HT3 receptors in the chemoreceptor trigger zone
Activation of motilin receptors on gastric smooth muscle
Blockade of muscarinic receptors in the basal ganglia
Excess serotonin activity from 5-HT4 receptor stimulation
questions.explanation: The drug is **metoclopramide**, a **D2 antagonist** used for diabetic gastroparesis. Blocking D2 receptors in the **nigrostriatal pathway** causes **extrapyramidal effects**: acute dystonia within days, and **tardive dyskinesia** with long use. Metoclopramide also stimulates 5-HT4 receptors, but **serotonin syndrome** would cause fever, clonus and diarrhea, which she does not have. Acute dystonia is treated with an **anticholinergic** (benztropine or diphenhydramine), so muscarinic blockade relieves it rather than causing it.
questions.explanation_pt: O medicamento é a **metoclopramida**, um **antagonista D2** usado na gastroparesia diabética. O bloqueio D2 na **via nigroestriatal** causa **efeitos extrapiramidais**: distonia aguda em poucos dias e **discinesia tardia** com o uso prolongado. A metoclopramida também estimula receptores 5-HT4, mas a **síndrome serotoninérgica** causaria febre, clônus e diarreia, que ela não tem. A distonia aguda é tratada com **anticolinérgico** (benzatropina ou difenidramina), então o bloqueio muscarínico alivia o quadro em vez de causá-lo.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old man with ulcerative colitis has been in remission for 3 years on an oral drug. He also takes a daily folic acid supplement. He and his wife have tried to conceive for 14 months, and her evaluation is normal. His testes are normal in size. FSH, LH and testosterone are normal. Semen analysis shows a low sperm count with poor motility. Which drug is he most likely taking?
choices: Mesalamine
Infliximab
Budesonide
Azathioprine
Sulfasalazine
questions.explanation: **Sulfasalazine** is split by colonic bacteria into **5-ASA** (the active anti-inflammatory part) and **sulfapyridine**. Sulfapyridine causes most of its adverse effects, such as reversible **oligospermia**, rash and **hemolysis in G6PD deficiency**, and the drug also lowers **folate** absorption. The most tempting distractor is mesalamine, but it is 5-ASA alone, without the sulfonamide carrier, and it is not linked to low sperm counts. Switching to mesalamine usually restores sperm counts.
questions.explanation_pt: A **sulfassalazina** é clivada pelas bactérias do cólon em **5-ASA** (a parte anti-inflamatória ativa) e **sulfapiridina**. A sulfapiridina causa a maioria dos efeitos adversos, como **oligospermia** reversível, exantema e **hemólise na deficiência de G6PD**, e o fármaco também reduz a absorção de **folato**. O distrator mais tentador é a mesalazina, mas ela é apenas o 5-ASA, sem o carreador sulfonamídico, e não está associada a contagem baixa de espermatozoides. A troca por mesalazina costuma normalizar a contagem.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis takes naproxen every day. Last year she had a bleeding gastric ulcer; testing for Helicobacter pylori was negative. She needs to continue the NSAID. Her physician plans to add misoprostol to prevent another ulcer. Before starting this drug, which of the following is most important to confirm?
choices: Normal serum magnesium level
Negative pregnancy test
Normal QT interval on ECG
Normal G6PD activity
Normal TPMT activity
questions.explanation: **Misoprostol** is a **PGE1 analog**. It replaces the mucosal prostaglandins that NSAIDs block: it raises mucus and bicarbonate secretion and lowers acid secretion. It also makes the uterus contract, so it can cause **abortion** and is **contraindicated in pregnancy**; women of childbearing age need a negative test and reliable contraception. Its most common adverse effect is **diarrhea**. G6PD activity matters for sulfasalazine and TPMT activity for azathioprine, not for misoprostol.
questions.explanation_pt: O **misoprostol** é um **análogo da PGE1**. Repõe as prostaglandinas da mucosa que os AINEs bloqueiam: aumenta a secreção de muco e bicarbonato e reduz a secreção ácida. Também causa contração uterina, por isso pode provocar **aborto** e é **contraindicado na gestação**; mulheres em idade fértil precisam de teste negativo e contracepção eficaz. Seu efeito adverso mais comum é a **diarreia**. A atividade de G6PD importa para a sulfassalazina e a de TPMT para a azatioprina, não para o misoprostol.

notes.title: GI pharmacology: acid, nausea, bowel and IBD drugs
notes.body_md:
## Acid and the mucosa

- **H2 blockers** (famotidine, cimetidine): block parietal cell H2 receptors. **Cimetidine** inhibits **CYP450** and is **antiandrogenic** (gynecomastia).
- **PPIs** (omeprazole, pantoprazole): **irreversibly** block the **H+/K+ ATPase**. Long-term risks: *C. difficile*, fractures, **hypomagnesemia**, pneumonia, low **iron** and **B12** absorption. Stopping can cause rebound acid.
- **Antacids**: aluminum (constipation, low phosphate), magnesium (diarrhea; toxic in renal failure), calcium (hypercalcemia, milk-alkali syndrome).
- **Sucralfate**: needs acid to coat the ulcer base. **Bismuth**: coats ulcers, used against *H. pylori*, turns stool and tongue black.
- **Misoprostol**: **PGE1 analog** that prevents NSAID ulcers. Diarrhea; **contraindicated in pregnancy**.

## Nausea and motility

- **Ondansetron**: **5-HT3 antagonist**; headache, constipation, QT prolongation.
- **Metoclopramide**: **D2 antagonist** and prokinetic; **extrapyramidal effects**, **tardive dyskinesia**. Avoid in **bowel obstruction** and **Parkinson disease**.
- **Prochlorperazine** (mainly D2 blocker) and **promethazine** (mainly H1 blocker): sedation.
- **Aprepitant**: **NK1 antagonist** for chemotherapy vomiting. **Dronabinol**: cannabinoid for nausea and appetite.

## Bowel

- **Osmotic**: **lactulose** (also traps ammonia in hepatic encephalopathy), polyethylene glycol, magnesium salts.
- **Stimulant**: senna, bisacodyl. **Bulk-forming**: psyllium.
- **Loperamide** and **diphenoxylate**: opioid agonists; avoid in invasive colitis and severe IBD (**toxic megacolon**).
- **Rifaximin**: hepatic encephalopathy and traveler's diarrhea.

## IBD

- **Sulfasalazine**: 5-ASA plus **sulfapyridine**; oligospermia, folate deficiency, hemolysis in G6PD deficiency. **Mesalamine** is 5-ASA alone.
- **Azathioprine / 6-MP**: purine analogs; **allopurinol** raises their toxicity.
- **Infliximab**: anti-TNF; screen for latent **TB** and hepatitis B first.

## Other

- **Octreotide**: varices, carcinoid, VIPoma, acromegaly; **gallstones**.
- **Ursodiol**: dissolves **cholesterol stones**; treats **primary biliary cholangitis**.
- **Pancreatic enzymes** treat exocrine insufficiency (chronic pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis).
notes.body_pt_md:
## Ácido e mucosa

- **Bloqueadores H2** (famotidina, cimetidina): bloqueiam receptores H2 das células parietais. A **cimetidina** inibe o **CYP450** e é **antiandrogênica** (ginecomastia).
- **IBPs** (omeprazol, pantoprazol): bloqueiam de forma **irreversível** a **H+/K+ ATPase**. Riscos no uso prolongado: *C. difficile*, fraturas, **hipomagnesemia**, pneumonia, menor absorção de **ferro** e **B12**. A suspensão pode causar rebote ácido.
- **Antiácidos**: alumínio (constipação, fosfato baixo), magnésio (diarreia; tóxico na insuficiência renal), cálcio (hipercalcemia, síndrome leite-álcali).
- **Sucralfato**: precisa de ácido para recobrir a base da úlcera. **Bismuto**: recobre úlceras, usado contra *H. pylori*, escurece fezes e língua.
- **Misoprostol**: **análogo da PGE1** que previne úlceras por AINEs. Diarreia; **contraindicado na gestação**.

## Náusea e motilidade

- **Ondansetrona**: **antagonista 5-HT3**; cefaleia, constipação, prolongamento do QT.
- **Metoclopramida**: **antagonista D2** e procinético; **efeitos extrapiramidais**, **discinesia tardia**. Evitar na **obstrução intestinal** e na **doença de Parkinson**.
- **Proclorperazina** (principalmente bloqueador D2) e **prometazina** (principalmente bloqueador H1): sedação.
- **Aprepitanto**: **antagonista NK1** para vômitos da quimioterapia. **Dronabinol**: canabinoide para náusea e apetite.

## Intestino

- **Osmóticos**: **lactulose** (também retém amônia na encefalopatia hepática), polietilenoglicol, sais de magnésio.
- **Estimulantes**: sene, bisacodil. **Formadores de bolo fecal**: psyllium.
- **Loperamida** e **difenoxilato**: agonistas opioides; evitar na colite invasiva e na DII grave (**megacólon tóxico**).
- **Rifaximina**: encefalopatia hepática e diarreia do viajante.

## DII

- **Sulfassalazina**: 5-ASA mais **sulfapiridina**; oligospermia, deficiência de folato, hemólise na deficiência de G6PD. A **mesalazina** é só o 5-ASA.
- **Azatioprina / 6-MP**: análogos de purina; o **alopurinol** aumenta sua toxicidade.
- **Infliximabe**: anti-TNF; rastrear **tuberculose** latente e hepatite B antes.

## Outros

- **Octreotida**: varizes, carcinoide, VIPoma, acromegalia; **cálculos biliares**.
- **Ácido ursodesoxicólico**: dissolve **cálculos de colesterol**; trata a **colangite biliar primária**.
- **Enzimas pancreáticas** tratam a insuficiência exócrina (pancreatite crônica, fibrose cística).
